title.narrative: EU TEI Inclusive Economic Development Guatemala
EU TEI Inkluderande Ekonomisk Utveckling Guatemala

description.narrative:
General objective Expanded the availability of financial services and products for SMEs, legal entities, and entrepreneurs, to venture and compete in markets and contribute to poverty reduction, human development, improvement of livelihoods and the stimulation of inclusive economic growth with emphasis on rural population and women.
Specific Objectives 1. Strengthened the identified local financial institutions and cooperatives, through technical assistance and training processes to improve their capacity to provide monetary and nonmonetary financial services that are adapted to the needs of SMEs and entrepreneurs, with a gender perspective. 2. Promoted the strengthening of SMEs and entrepreneurs to increase their financial inclusion, and the empowerment and financial inclusion of rural women both as users of financial services and owners of SMEs. 3. Innovative solutions promoted to facilitate the mobilization of private resources and attract new actors to the rural financial ecosystem to develop solutions to the challenges identified during the implementation of specific objectives 1 and 2, using the "Challenge fund" mechanism. With emphasis on rural indigenous women, entrepreneurs and returned migrants.

Bidraget ska stimulera ekonomisk tillväxt, öka synergier mellan handel och utvecklingssamarbete genom att stärka små och medelstora företag, utnyttja medel genom en utmaningsfond, öka hållbart företagande, stödja innovation och digitalisering.

The contribution shall stimulate economic growth, increase synergies between trade and development cooperation by strengthening SMEs, leverage funds through a challenge fund, increase sustainable entrepreneurships, support innovation and digitalization.

Swisscontact developed the following strategies to guide the provision of targeted technical assistance services to involved cooperatives:
-(i) climate risk management, with a particular focus on agricultural loan portfolios that are highly exposed to climate variability. (ii) Data-driven decision-making: the project planned the establishment of Business Intelligence & Analytics (BIA) units to improve the use of data for strategic and operational decisions. (iii) Customer profiling: implementation of customer profiling systems was prioritized to better tailor financial products and services to rural populations. (iv) Digital connectivity: expanding digital connectivity was identified as a structural requirement to enable technology adoption and extend institutional outreach. (v) to strengthen institutional policies related to gender equity and engagement of vulnerable populations.
- During the reporting period, 35 rural SMEs received training on developing bankable business plans, including business formalization, financial analysis, cost management, and marketing. In parallel, the project advanced the development of a digital financial education curriculum delivered through digital platforms and AI-enabled chatbots, expanding rural entrepreneurs access to financial knowledge without reliance on physical infrastructure.
- The first edition of the Challenge Fund was successfully launched to promote digital financial innovation. From 25 proposals submitted by private sector institutions, four initiatives were selected: Carla (Fintech): Delivers financial services via WhatsApp, including identity verification, digital signatures, and conversational assistants, broadening access for rural users with limited connectivity. Fibbo (Fintech): Automates invoice management and enables digital factoring, allowing SMEs to convert invoices into liquidity and improve cash flow. AGROCLIMÁTICA (Agrotech): Provides climate risk analysis for crops and territories, supporting financial institutions in tailoring credit products and safeguarding agricultural portfolios. Bowpi (Fintech): Digitizes the full credit cycle from application and verification to approval and disbursement helping cooperatives streamline operations and expand rural outreach.
The challenge fund awarded USD 358,000 in grants and leveraged an additional USD 182,000 in co financing to support solutions focused on cooperative interoperability, intelligent portfolio segmentation, climate risk management, and SME's factoring services.
- Guarantee Instrument: The project contributed to optimize the Sida's guarantee mechanisms implemented by COSAMI and COOPSAMA, through four key actions: (i) the design of COSAMIs Women Credit product, scheduled for launch in 2026; (ii) the development of a financial strategy for returned migrants, including analysis of 48 loan applications from refugees and asylum seekers; (iii) the rollout of a Business Intelligence & Analytics (BIA) process expected to increase guarantee placement efficiency by up to 25% by 2027; and (iv) the signing of eight strategic MoUs with national partners to mobilize technical and financial resources for vulnerable populations.
All mentioned interventions are aligned with the EU Global Gateway strategy and its Green and Digital Transition priorities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
